lead.headline: Congo will halt cobalt exports again from Nov 30 as prices slide and stockpiles build
lead.dek: The world's largest cobalt supplier is swapping its quota for a full suspension with no end date, to be reviewed after four months. In northern Thailand, arsenic linked to mining across the border has more than 20,000 households on trucked water.
body: Congo's strategic minerals regulator, ARECOMS, will suspend all cobalt exports from Nov 30, 2026, until further notice, SMM reported on Nov 23, citing Bloomberg. The decision was adopted at a Nov 9 meeting and covers industrial and artisanal mines, The Northern Miner reported. The regulator cited a sharp fall in prices since June, slower consumption growth, rising inventories and speculation, and said it will reassess after four months and revise how export quotas are allocated in the meantime.

It is Congo's second halt. The country supplied about three quarters of the world's mined cobalt before it first stopped shipments in February 2025, then switched to quotas in October 2025 with a 2026 ceiling of 96,600 tonnes. Cobalt hydroxide in Asia was $14.50 a pound of contained cobalt on Oct 14, down 43% since July 1, the Cobalt Institute said, citing Benchmark data. China's CMOC produced 99,694 tonnes of cobalt in the first nine months of 2026 but sold 12,661 tonnes, while Glencore's output fell by more than half to 13,700 tonnes.

Supply controls are tightening elsewhere too. Thailand plans to stop exporting chemicals used in rare earth mining to Myanmar after river contamination in its north, Reuters reported Nov 23. Vietnam broke ground the same day on a $60 million plant in Hai Phong to separate 10,000 tonnes a year of rare earth oxides from late 2028. And USA Rare Earth told the SEC that Brazil's new critical minerals law, whose rules are not yet written, could affect its Serra Verde operations.

nexus.electrons: Battery and magnet supply chains feel each control first. Niron Magnetics plans a $1.8 billion iron nitride magnet plant in Alabama, an alternative to neodymium magnets, with output from 2029.
nexus.molecules: Mining runs on reagents. Thailand's deputy prime minister said on Nov 21 it would block exports of rare earth mining chemicals to Myanmar and other relevant countries, Reuters reported.
nexus.pore: Some supply comes from the subsurface instead of a pit. Element3's Midland, Texas plant has extracted lithium from Permian produced water since February 2026, using Oak Ridge licensed technology.
nexus.water: Thai authorities are trucking water to more than 20,000 households after arsenic reached 30 times the safe limit in Mae Sai tap water, Al Jazeera reported. Naresuan University traced much of the Sai River sediment to gold mining in Myanmar.

use.text: Cobalt price support now depends on a ban with no end date. Watch the four month review and CMOC's unsold stock.
Export controls, reagent bans and investment screening are converging. Map which apply to each supply route.
Battery makers should check cobalt contracts for force majeure and origin terms before Nov 30.
Rare earth free magnets and brine lithium are drawing capital. Proof of cost at scale is still ahead.

briefs.headline: Niron plans a $1.8 billion rare earth free magnet complex in Alabama as rare earth stocks rebound
briefs.text: Niron Magnetics plans to invest $1.8 billion in a permanent magnet complex in Dothan, Alabama, its second site, SMM reported Nov 24. Construction is expected to begin in 2028, with production from 2029 at 10,000 tonnes a year of iron nitride magnets, an alternative to neodymium magnets, for AI, automotive, defence and industrial buyers; about 700 jobs are expected. Rare earth stocks rallied with the wider market on Monday: USA Rare Earth rose 13% to $7.09 and MP Materials 6% to $35.98 in afternoon trading, 24/7 Wall St. reported, though both remain down for the year. On its Nov 5 call MP said it does not expect today's elevated prices for several medium and heavy rare earths to persist indefinitely.

use.text: A 2028 construction start means years of execution risk. Weigh it against magnet price floors in existing offtakes.
Ask for test data on iron nitride performance in your duty cycle before planning a switch.

briefs.headline: Thailand moves to cut off mining chemicals to Myanmar as arsenic reaches its taps
briefs.text: Thailand plans to stop exporting chemicals used in rare earth mining to Myanmar amid cross border pollution, Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said on Saturday, Reuters reported. The government also plans to designate the Thai side of the Kok River a pollution control zone. Authorities are supplying clean water to more than 20,000 households after arsenic in Mae Sai district's waterworks reached 30 times the safe limit and untreated Sai River water 25 times the drinking water limit, Al Jazeera and AFP reported Nov 18. Researchers at Naresuan University traced much of the Sai River's arsenic laden sediment to gold mining in Myanmar. A joint Thai and Myanmar working group meets on Nov 25 and 26, The Nation reported, and Reuters said Thailand, China and Myanmar plan talks from Nov 24 to 26.

use.text: Ask suppliers whether feedstock traces to Shan or Kachin State mines. Pollution claims are becoming a trade issue.
Upstream mining can outrun treatment. Arsenic monitoring and backup sources are the near term response.

briefs.headline: California offers up to $18 million for geothermal exploration and drilling
briefs.text: California will make up to $18 million available through the California Energy Commission for geothermal exploration and drilling, with a competitive solicitation opening in January 2027, the state said Nov 23. Three to four projects are expected to win $4.5 million to $6 million each, and applicants must match at least 100% of the state money, so at least $36 million in total is expected. The Department of Conservation is putting $1.1 million into resource mapping and will start an overhaul of geothermal well rules in early December, which it called the most comprehensive in more than 50 years. A public workshop is set for Dec 15 and awards for May or June 2027.

use.text: Line up matching capital now; the 100% match is the gate.
Comment on the well rule overhaul in December; it sets technical terms for decades.

briefs.headline: Canada opens a carbon removal buying program to 19 offers, but nothing is bought yet
briefs.text: Canada's Treasury Board announced a national master standing offer on Nov 19 with 19 offers from 17 suppliers across five categories: direct air capture with storage (4), BECCS (3), biochar (5), other biomass removal (4) and enhanced mineralization (3), The Deep Dive reported. A standing offer is not a contract; federal bodies must issue call ups before purchases bind. Ottawa has pledged at least C$10 million of removal purchases by 2030, about $7 million, Argus reported. Remova Carbon Systems of Calgary holds half the potential BECCS dollars for a plant near Whitecourt, Alberta, targeting about 20,000 tonnes a year from 2028. The offers run to March 31, 2029, with an option to 2031.

use.text: A place on the standing offer is a sales channel, not revenue. Target departments with fleet emissions.
Government category splits are a useful benchmark for portfolio mixes.

briefs.headline: Negotiators say Saudi Arabia led resistance to fossil fuel wording at COP31
briefs.text: Negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa told Reuters that Saudi Arabia was at the forefront of resisting language on reducing reliance on fossil fuels at COP31, the main reason no political agreement was reached, Dawn reported Nov 24. About 130 countries had backed a proposal that any deal mention transitioning away from fossil fuels and drop the reference to carbon capture, Reuters and Carbon Herald reported. The failed text had set at least 500 million tonnes a year of capture capacity by 2035. The Turkish presidency said no group or country received preferential treatment; Saudi representatives did not immediately comment.

use.text: Capture is now politically coded in UN talks. Expect buyers and lenders to ask how projects relate to fossil output.
Bonn in June 2027 is the next chance to revisit the wording.

research.title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centers
research.by: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Nature Sustainability
research.text: Satellite imagery found 403 hyperscale sites using 68 to 99 TWh from May 2024 to April 2025, about 1.8% of US electricity and 25.7 Mt of CO2; about 54% of the power was fossil generated.

research.title: Ocean takes a growing share of carbon emissions while land absorption stalls
research.by: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, Science
research.text: Thirty years of O2 and CO2 records show the ocean took up 2.8 billion tonnes of CO2 a year from 1990 to 2019, about 35% of fossil emissions, while the land sink peaked around 2009 and has generally declined.

research.title: Tracing arsenic in the Sai River
research.by: Naresuan University, reported by Al Jazeera and AFP
research.text: Chemical analysis and satellite modelling traced much of the arsenic laden sediment in the Sai River, a Mekong tributary, to gold mining across the border in Myanmar.

minerals.intro: Producers are reaching for controls as prices fall: Congo moves from a cobalt quota to a full export halt on Nov 30, Thailand targets reagents for Myanmar's rare earth mines, and new processing capacity breaks ground in Vietnam.

items.name: Cobalt
items.headline: Congo suspends cobalt exports from Nov 30, with a review after four months
items.text: ARECOMS adopted the suspension on Nov 9, citing a sharp price fall since June, slower consumption and rising inventories, and will revise quota allocation during the halt, SMM and The Northern Miner reported Nov 23. The 2026 export ceiling had been 96,600 tonnes. Cobalt hydroxide was $14.50 a pound on Oct 14, down 43% since July 1.

items.name: Rare earths
items.headline: Vietnam breaks ground on a $60 million rare earth oxide plant in Hai Phong
items.text: Khanh An Industrial Park JSC began building a 14 hectare plant with five hydrometallurgical separation lines and 10,000 tonnes a year of capacity for individual oxides above 99% purity, TNGlobal reported Nov 23. Prime Minister Le Minh Hung attended; commercial operation is set from Q4 2028.

items.name: Rare earths policy
items.headline: Thailand to block rare earth mining chemicals to Myanmar; USA Rare Earth flags Brazil law
items.text: Thailand will stop exporting chemicals used in rare earth mining to Myanmar over river pollution, Reuters reported Nov 23. Separately, USA Rare Earth told the SEC that Brazil's Law 15,506/2026, which lets future rules set export conditions and screen foreign control, could affect its Serra Verde mine; no restriction is in place yet, The Rio Times reported.

items.name: Uranium
items.headline: Cyberattack disrupts Peninsula Energy's Lance uranium mine in Wyoming
items.text: Peninsula said a Nov 20 cyberattack hit Lance's operating server and requested an ASX trading halt; corporate systems were unaffected and it has not said whether production stopped, The Northern Miner reported Nov 23. It had already withdrawn its 2026 target of 400,000 to 500,000 lb U3O8 because of low well flows.

items.name: Lithium
items.headline: Permian produced water becomes a lithium source in Midland, Texas
items.text: Element3's plant in Midland started up in February 2026 and makes battery grade lithium carbonate from oilfield produced water using technology licensed from Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Industrial Info reported. It is not yet at capacity. The US produces under 1% of world lithium, per USGS.
